svg.title: Child poverty fell to 5.1 percent in 2021, the lowest since the series began in 2009, and more than doubled the next year.
svg.desc: Line chart of child poverty under the Supplemental Poverty Measure, 2009 to 2025, with the official measure in gray. It fell from 17.0 percent in 2009 to 5.1 percent in 2021, the year the expanded child tax credit was paid, rose to 12.0 percent in 2022 and stood at 13.4 percent in 2025, where both measures meet. Set in Inter and Inter Tight. Without both fonts installed, the labels set in another font and change width.

text.tspan: 2021: the expanded child tax credit was
in force, and it lapsed after that year.
The timing alone does not show how
much of the drop came from the credit.
Both measures: 13.4% in 2025. In July 2025, Public Law
119-21 set the child tax credit at up to $2,200 per child, at
most $1,700 of it refundable and only above $2,500 in
